source_title: LMT Onsrud Laminated Chipboard Cutting Data Recommendations (catalog page 119, upper table)
coverage_notes: NEW source (linked from https://www.onsrud.com/Forms/Cutting-Data-Recommendations.asp). The PDF is the whole catalog page 119: its text layer holds BOTH the Laminated Chipboard and the Laminated Plywood tables (the Laminated Plywood PDF is the same page, another crop, another sha). Depth rule: 'Greater than 3 x D, reduce chip load by 25%'. Prints 37-00/37-20, 37-50, 37-60, 37-80 and flat series 48-000, 57-200, 57-200MD, 60-100MW/C/MC/PLR, 60-600, 68-100. The 37-60 row sits under 3/8, 9/16 and 7/8 in (render-checked), which matches no 37-60 catalog size: probable layout error, transcribed as printed. No ball nose, no tapered ball. Candidate rows from this source: 10.

source_title: Amana Polycrystalline Diamond (PCD) Ball Nose Router Bit Speed Chart v2
coverage_notes: NEW source. PCD ball nose DRB-432 (1/4 in) and DRB-433 (3/8 in), 2 teeth, rows CFRP, Plastics, Wood, MDF, Chipboard Without Coating, with chipload and RPM ranges printed in inch and mm. The only printed ball-nose chart found with a chipboard (particleboard) row. MDF band is BELOW the Wood band on both sizes (1/4: MDF .0016-.005 vs Wood .002-.007; 3/8: MDF .005-.008 vs Wood .006-.01); Chipboard equals Wood. No plywood row. PCD, not carbide. Candidate rows from this source: 4.

source_title: Leitz Lexicon Edition 7, 05 Routing (Version 3, 05/2026)
coverage_notes: Target 2 statements, no rows. Stored text is an EXCERPT: only the pages that print 'Correction factor for vf'. Each vf diagram names a base 'Workpiece material' at a fixed speed n; the factor scales vf for another material. Base plastic-coated chipboard: 'MDF = 0.8' (most diagrams), 'MDF = 0.9' (jointing), 'MDF = 0.6' (one diagram), 'Uncoated chipboard = 1.1', 'Solid wood = 0.8' (grooving), 'Pre trimming MDF = 1.2'. Base softwood (sizing/jointing): 'Hardwood = 0.8; Chipboard = 1.3; Glulam = 0.9', 'Hardwood = 0.8; Chipboard = 1.2', 'Hardwood = 0.9; ... Chipboard = 1.1', 'Hardwood = 0.7; Glulam = 0.8'. NO plywood factor anywhere in the volume. Tools are industrial sizing/grooving/jointing cutters (straight, turnblade, diamond), not ball nose or V-bit. Reading a vf factor at fixed n and Z as an fz factor is an inference (derived). Candidate rows from this source: 0.
